title: Mackinnon:
title_short: V21 · Why I Trust This Model
headline: She watched money disappear in big systems. Then she found a model where every dollar reaches care, and you hear what happens.
story: Someone asked Mackinnon why she joined Watsi. She spent years in the UN and big NGOs and watched funding disappear into systems.
Then the turn: “Then I met Watsi.” A simple chain from patient to donor. 100% to care. And honesty, even when surgery does not go as planned. Calm, sure, warm. It ends on connection, not on numbers.
do: Open on frame 1 with “Why did you join Watsi?” on top.
Start the music on “Then I met Watsi”, not before.
Keep the honesty line plain and steady.
One brand touch only: the underline under 100%.
End before “How do you feel? Good.”
dont: No title card or logo at 0:00.
No sad tone on the “surgery doesn't always go as planned” line.
No stats graphics. The captions carry the numbers.

bp_intro: All source times are in Mincho5163.MP4 (1:20, one 4K camera, Mackinnon only). Times come from the transcript.json and are accurate to about 0.2 s. Find exact in and out points on the waveform. Every frame is from the real file. The yellow box shows the 9:16 crop.

rows.frame_alt: Mackinnon in a beige blouse, dark green wall, curtain on the left
rows.visual: Mackinnon, wide and locked-off. In-point on “Someone”.
rows.motion: Question on top from frame 1, top third: Why did you join Watsi? (her own words). Lato Bold, Watsi yellow #FFCC33, soft shadow. Cut on. Stays to 00:05.5. Captions start with her voice.

voice.quote: Someone asked me why I joined Watsi.

rows.visual: Same shot. Keep her pauses between “Overhead. Bureaucracy.” Small 2% push-in across the line.
rows.motion: Question fades out at 00:05.5 (6 frames). Name super “Mackinnon” at 00:06–00:08, lower left, above the captions, large. First name only.

voice.quote: I'd spent years in huge organizations, the UN, big NGOs, organizations that do important work, genuinely, but I'd also watched a lot of funding disappear into systems, overhead, bureaucracy, the gap between the dollar that was given and the person who needed it. It could have done so much good.

rows.frame_alt: Mackinnon opens her hands: “Then I met Watsi”
rows.visual: Back to 100% with a hard cut on “Then I met Watsi”. This is the turn.
rows.motion: Captions only. The transcript writes “WOTC”. It is Watsi.

voice.quote: Then I met Watsi, and the model is simple in the best possible way. A patient needs care, we share their story, donors give, the money goes to the hospital, patient receives treatment, and donors always know their impact.

rows.music: Music enters on “Then I met Watsi”. Warm, sustained piano or guitar bed, 18–20 dB under her voice. No drums.

rows.frame_alt: Mackinnon with one arm out, explaining
rows.motion: Brand touch (the only one): a hand-drawn underline from the September Spirit “Extras” set draws under the caption word “100%” in 8 frames, Watsi cyan #11BAED. Holds 1 s, then off. Captions write “100%” and “90%” as numbers.

voice.quote: That's it, 100% of donations go to care, not 90%, not most of it, every dollar, and you hear what happens.

rows.visual: Back to 100%. Plain and steady. This line is honesty, not sadness: no slow push, no music dip.

voice.quote: Even when the outcome isn't what we hoped for, surgery doesn't always go as planned, and we share those stories too. And I also think that's what helps build trust, not pretending that every story has a perfect ending, but being honest about what happens.

rows.music: Bed steady. Do not drop it here.

voice.quote: I trust this model because I've seen it work thousands of times in dozens of countries for patients and donors who have never met and will never meet and are nonetheless connected in a real way.

rows.music: Small lift on “connected”. Not a swell.

rows.visual: On her. Hold 0.7 s after “world”. Out before “How do you feel? Good.” (01:18.88).

voice.quote: That connection is what we do, and it's a dream to be building it with our team and our community around the world.

rows.visual: Clean end card. Light cyan #D3EDFA background. Navy is never a background.
rows.motion: watsi.org, all lowercase, Lato, navy #2E2844. One line. Nothing under it. No stats, no donate button.

Uppbeat, like other Watsi cuts. Save the license certificate with the project: YouTube flagged an Uppbeat track on a Watsi upload on 7 Oct.
tech: 3840×2160, 23.976 fps, H.264, 2-ch audio recorded into the camera
1080×1920 at 23.976 fps. Same as the source. No frame-rate change.
A 9:16 crop of 4K is 1215×2160, so it is sharper than 1080×1920. Punch-ins up to 112% stay native. The room is dim: lift exposure and skin a little, keep it natural.
2 channels recorded into the camera. Pick the live channel on the waveform and map it to both sides. Mute the other. (Not measured: the Drive download limit stopped the audio check.)
Lato Bold, white, soft shadow, large. Pop word by word. No highlight box, no shading block. One line at a time. Always on screen, also in pauses. Keep the bottom 20% clear for app buttons.
checklist: Read every caption against the audio. Sonam checks every word, and typos are her top complaint.
The transcript writes “WOTC”. It is Watsi, capital W only. The URL is watsi.org, all lowercase.
The question is on screen from frame 1 and stays at least 5 seconds.
Name super “Mackinnon” is large, first name only, and never at 0:00.
Captions never drop out, even in pauses.
Keep her natural pauses. The delivery must sound like her, not a teleprompter.
Only one brand element on screen at a time.
Every “WOTC” in the transcript is captioned Watsi. “100%” and “90%” are numbers.
client_note: Why this matters: trust and transparency is Watsi's 2026 theme. This is Mackinnon saying it in her own words. Evergreen: it can also go to donor emails, LinkedIn and conference intros.
